jobs.description: Employer: Vermont Natural Resources Council Expires: 10/30/2026 Would you like to learn about the legislative process, tracking issues related to climate, housing, community planning, transportation, environmental justice, water, forests and wildlife in Vermont?VNRC and our partners, Vermont Conservation Voters (VCV) and the Vermont Planners Association (VPA) are seeking a Legislative Intern to help track forward-looking environmental legislation moving through the State House during the 2027 legislative session (January through April 2027). jobs.description: Employer: Mars, Inc. Expires: 10/30/2026 At Mars, we work together to build a better world for people, pets, and the planet. From being a socially responsible business, to investing in our Associates, we're always looking at how we can make tomorrow brighter. Being on-site also enables interns to build relationships with our experts, expand their professional networks, and fully immerse themselves in the R&D environment. Some pretty sweet perks including competitive salary & benefits package, fun freebies, and pet-friendly offices. Location of the internship will be focused in the Chicago area locations with potential short-term travel to other sites including Battle Creek, Michigan About Mars, Incorporated For more than a century, Mars, Incorporated has been driven by the belief that the world we want tomorrow starts with how we do business today. The Mars Five Principles – Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency and Freedom – inspire our Associates to take action every day to help create a world tomorrow in which the planet, its people and pets can thrive. The Mars Compass, inspired by the Economics of Mutuality, is used to measure the company’s progress in service of its purpose; The world we want tomorrow starts with how we do business today. jobs.description: Employer: Western National Insurance Group Expires: 10/30/2026 Who are we?Western National Insurance Group is a private mutual insurance company with over 120 years of experience serving customers' property-and-casualty insurance needs in the Midwestern, Northwestern, and Southwestern United States. Our company growth, combined with our focus on innovation, transformation, and investments in the customer experience are key drivers supporting the expansion of our team. You will work alongside experienced data engineers and business partners while learning about enterprise data warehousing, data integration, software development, and Agile delivery practices. Potential responsibilities include:Work with technologies used in our data environment, including SQL Server, SSIS, Snowflake, Python, and other tools that support enterprise data warehousing and automation. Our team is also transitioning selected data workloads from SSIS and SQL Server toward Snowflake, providing exposure to both established and modern data engineering practices.Develop and test enhancements to data applications, ETL/ELT workflows, and supporting processes based on business requirements.Troubleshoot and debug data integration and Enterprise Data Warehousing (EDW) issues by analyzing data, reviewing code, and working with team members to identify solutions.Write clear, maintainable code and contribute to code reviews, unit testing, and other quality practices.Participate in Agile activities such as backlog refinement, work estimation, planning, and team discussions.Help identify opportunities to improve data processes, documentation, automation, and team efficiency.Create and maintain technical documentation to support learning, onboarding, ongoing maintenance, and production releases.Follow data security, privacy, quality, and change-management practices appropriate for an insurance environment.Complete special projects and other duties as assigned. What You’ll Need to Succeed:Currently pursuing a degree, certificate, or coursework in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Information Systems, Mathematics, or a related field.A passion for technology and an interest in working with, analyzing, and improving data.Basic experience with SQL and relational databases through coursework, projects, employment, or personal learning.Exposure to Python or another scripting/programming language.Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, with an interest in understanding how systems and processes work.Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts to both technical and nontechnical audiences.Willingness to ask questions, learn from feedback, and collaborate effectively with others.Ability to pay close attention to detail when working with data, code, and documentation.Familiarity with Agile software development practices, source control tools such as Git or GitLab, or ETL/ELT technologies such as SSIS or Snowflake is preferred but not required.Exposure to DevOps concepts, CI/CD processes, testing practices, or tools such as Docker or Jenkins is a plus.Two years of college or equivalent relevant experience is preferred. Strong applicants will be proficient in Excel and Google Workspace, may have customer service or call center experience, and have a general knowledge of politics within Minnesota. Key responsibilities include:Data Management: Work with Finance Team to maintain accurate and up to date data on donors and donor outreach.Donor Relations: Work with the Finance Team to grow our grassroots donor program on all levels. Applicants with good working knowledge of Excel encouraged to apply.Party Affairs:The Minnesota DFL seeks two interns to assist in the Party Affairs department. The Party Affairs Department supports the work of the local and statewide volunteer committees. jobs.title: 2027 Marketing Internship at Polaris Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Polaris Inc. Expires: 10/30/2026 Marketing Internship - Summer 2027 Company Overview Polaris Inc. is a global leader in powersports and known to millions of people around the world as we offer a diverse portfolio of products and services including boats, off-road vehicles, commercial vehicles, and more. Polaris pioneers’ product breakthroughs and enriching experiences and services, that have invited people to discover the joy of being outdoors since our founding in 1954. At Polaris, we have fun doing what we love by driving change and innovation. We empower employees to take on challenging assignments and roles with an elevated level of responsibility in our agile working environment. Our people make us who we are and help create incredible products and experiences that empower us to Think Outside. Internship Program Overview The Polaris Marketing Internship (MIP) is a tailored 12-week paid summer internship designed for emerging sophomores, juniors, and seniors who are interested in pursuing a career in a leading global powersports industry. As a Marketing Intern, you will be given impactful project-based assignments that directly align with business objectives. These projects could include exposure, within our marketing division, across various segments including targeted development in these areas: Brand and Product Marketing (Brand/Lifestyle Marketing, Insights and Analytics) How you create and capture through brand and product marketing Creative and Content (Social Media, Paid Media, Partnerships, Events) How Creative and Content Creation drives business today and tomorrow Process and Go-to-Market (Ecommerce, Digital Production) How Process, Planning and communication improve work Dealer and Channel (Channel, Retail, Owner Experience, In-Market and Key Market Impact) How Dealership and Sales Channels impact our business We encourage you to embrace the adventure and be open to any placement opportunity. Being mobile and flexible will allow you to gain diverse experiences and make the most of your internship. Internship Locations Could Include: Any Polaris location across the United States. This program serves as a primary feeder into our rotational leadership development program, providing you as an intern with the foundational skills and experiences needed to excel in your career. Upon completion of the internship program, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a passion to learn may be offered a returning internship or a full-time position, depending on eligibility. As a Polaris intern it is important that you embrace the adventure and remain open to any placement opportunity. By being adaptable, you will gain diverse experiences and develop a broader skill set, which are essential for your professional development and success within Polaris. Our internship program is crafted to build the foundational skills and experiences essential for your career success. Upon completing the internship, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a strong passion for learning may be offered a returning internship or a position in our rotational leadership development program. In addition to meaningful project work, you will participate in intentional programming and professional development offerings such as: Mentorship: you are paired with one of our DP associates for mentor support throughout your 12-weeks. Programming Hours: weekly functional and centralized learning sessions to broaden your knowledge base, both within and beyond your program. Networking: intentional time with peers and leaders at Polaris to build your professional network. Intern Innovation Challenge: internal case study designed to promote cross functional development where you and your team will present creative and practical solutions to a real ‘Polaris’ problem to our executive leadership. Early Talent Summit Week: you participate in our 3-day event in our Wyoming, MN office. This immersive experience brings together all US interns and DPs for professional development, structured networking, a DP graduation event, inspiring executive speakers, and a thrilling team ride on some of your favorite Polaris vehicles. Community Engagement: opportunity to get involved in your local community. Final Presentations: present to our senior level leaders to showcase your career aspirations and recap your internship experience. The Selection Process: Applications are open from August -November each year. Applications will be reviewed and shortlisted candidates will typically be contacted for an initial phone screen by the end of November. Candidates selected to move forward will be invited to participate in a virtual panel interview with an identified HR business partner and functional leader. Successful candidates would move forward to an offer. You will partner with the Early Talent team in January to complete a survey that provides a deeper look at your specific interests, strengths & career goals. All specific internship assignments are communicated in February, after aligning based on your specific interests and business demand. Intern Relocation Assistance: Polaris offers a relocation program for interns who qualify through our mobility vendor. To qualify for these services, your home address must be 35 miles or more from the office where you will be working. Benefits include a lump sum (grossed up to offset tax liability), access to a relocation counselor to explain the resources available to you and aid in securing short-term housing available to you. Your responsibilities will include daily transportation to/from the office. Required Qualifications: Pursuing a bachelor’s/ master’s degree in Marketing, Strategic Communications, or other related business degree with an emphasis in Marketing with an intended graduation date between August 2027-May 2029. Minimum overall GPA of 3.0 Must be able to commit to a full 12-week internship, working 40 hours per week, within one of the following date ranges: May 17th – August 6th, 2027. June 1st – August 20th, 2027. Willing and able to relocate. Must be a U.S. person (U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident, asylee, or refugee) and not require sponsorship for employment now or in the future. Must have reliable transportation for daily commuting to and from the office. Previous experience with Microsoft Office software tools (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams, and Word). Preferred Qualifications: Previous Internship/Co-op experience or involvement in relevant projects. Demonstrated strengths in analysis, creative problem-solving, communication, interpersonal relationships, self-motivation, and leadership. Strong interest in long-term career development and participation in leadership development programs. Previous leadership experience in work, organizations, or classroom. Completion of at least two years of university coursework Strong Communication (both written and verbal including strong presentation skills) Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, ever-changing, multi-tasking environment Strong organizational and project management skills This is more than an internship - It's the beginning of your career with Polaris. We hope you're ready for the ultimate adventure!

jobs.description: Employer: Apex Park and Recreation District Expires: 10/30/2026 Job Title: Intern – Golf InstructionDepartment: Golf Operations – Indian Tree Golf ClubSupervisor’s Title: Director of Golf and Clubhouse Operations/ Golf Instruction ProfessionalDate Prepared: 9/2026 Job Status: Part-Time, Non-Exempt POSITION PURPOSE: Supports golf instruction, player development, and related golf programming at Indian Tree Golf Club. Works alongside professional golf staff to gain hands-on experience assisting with junior and adult instruction, clinics, camps, individual lessons, player-development programs, and on-course instruction. Provides support for the administrative and operational responsibilities associated with delivering quality golf programming at a public golf facility. This internship is designed to provide meaningful professional development for an individual interested in pursuing a career in golf instruction, PGA Golf Management, recreation, sports management, or the golf industry. ESSENTIAL DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:Assists golf professionals with individual and group golf instruction for participants of varying ages and skill levels. Supports junior golf camps and clinics, adult programs, beginner programs, and other player-development initiatives. Assists with instruction in putting, chipping, pitching, bunker play, full swing, course management, rules, etiquette, and pace of play. Prepares instructional areas, equipment, training aids, range balls, and other materials prior to programs and lessons. Assists with participant check-in, group organization, instructional stations, and program transitions. Provides basic instructional feedback to participants under the direction of professional golf staff. Assists with on-course instruction on the Par-3 and regulation golf courses. Helps create a positive, encouraging, safe, and welcoming learning environment for golfers of different ages, abilities, skill levels, and backgrounds. Assists with adaptive golf and other programs designed to make golf accessible to a broad range of participants. Assists staff in developing golf clinics, camps, leagues, lesson plans, instructional activities, and other player-development opportunities. Helps evaluate existing programs and identifies opportunities to improve the participant experience. Supports player-development efforts for juniors, beginners, women, seniors, and other developing golfers. Assists with utilizing the driving range, practice facilities, and Par-3 course as player-development resources. Assists with program registration, participation tracking, attendance, participant feedback, and program evaluation. Supports marketing and communication efforts related to golf programs and instructional opportunities. Maintains clean, organized, safe, and professional instructional and practice areas. Consistently represents the Indian Tree Way – Intentional Hospitality, Operational Excellence, and Making It Work when interacting with participants, guests, and coworkers. OTHER DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:Gains exposure to golf shop operations, outside operations, tee-sheet management, pace of play, tournament operations, customer service, and daily golf course operations. Learns policies and procedures related to golf instruction, course access, range operations, safety, and guest service. Gains an understanding of golf program pricing, budgeting, revenue generation, expense management, and other business aspects of operating a public golf facility. Assists with golf shop and outside operations as assigned to gain a broader understanding of golf facility operations. Works with professional golf staff to establish internship learning goals and participates in ongoing coaching and feedback. May be given increasing responsibility for planning and delivering portions of clinics or instructional programs under the supervision of professional golf staff. Develops practical experience in golf instruction and coaching techniques, junior and adult programming, player development, customer service and hospitality, program management and evaluation, and public-sector golf operations. Performs other duties as assigned. SUPERVISORY DUTIES: This position does not have direct supervisory responsibilities. May assist with organizing and directing participants during camps, clinics, lessons, and other instructional activities under the supervision of professional golf staff. JOB QUALIFICATIONS -KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:Working knowledge of golf fundamentals, rules, etiquette, and pace of play. Interest in golf instruction, player development, golf operations, and the golf industry. Ability to effectively communicate with children, adults, guests, and coworkers. Strong customer service and interpersonal skills. Ability to create a positive and welcoming experience for program participants. Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. Ability to follow direction and work within the scope of assigned responsibilities and training. Ability and willingness to learn, accept coaching and feedback, and demonstrate initiative.Ability to maintain a professional appearance and demeanor. Ability to prioritize participant, guest, and employee safety. Ability to organize equipment and instructional materials and assist with multiple activities and participant groups. Ability to work a flexible schedule that may include mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays. Ability to consistently demonstrate the principles of the Indian Tree Way – Intentional Hospitality, Operational Excellence, and Making It Work. EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: Interest in golf instruction, PGA Golf Management, recreation, sports management, education, coaching, or a related field. Working knowledge of golf fundamentals, rules, and etiquette. Experience or demonstrated ability working effectively with children and adults. CPR/AED/First Aid certification or ability to obtain certification as required.Preferred Qualifications: Currently enrolled in or recently graduated from a PGA Golf Management, recreation, sports management, education, kinesiology, business, or related program. Previous experience working at a golf course, driving range, golf camp, recreation program, or instructional setting. Previous experience working with children or youth programs. Interest in pursuing PGA membership or a career in golf instruction, player development, or golf operations.WORK ENVIRONMENT: Work is performed in both indoor and outdoor environments at Indian Tree Golf Club, including the golf shop, driving range, practice facilities, Par-3 course, and regulation golf courses. Work may be performed in varying weather and environmental conditions. The position requires regular interaction with children, adults, program participants, guests, and other employees in an active public recreation environment.PHYSICAL ACTIVITIES: Position requires the ability to stand and walk for extended periods, including walking on uneven outdoor terrain and golf course surfaces. Requires frequent bending, reaching, and movement associated with demonstrating golf skills, setting up instructional areas, and assisting with programs. Must be able to handle, move, and set up golf equipment, training aids, range balls, and other instructional materials and equipment. TRAVEL: Limited travel may be required for meetings, training, programs, or other District-related activities. NOTE: This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications associated with the job. May perform other duties as assigned.

jobs.description: Employer: Deutsche Bank Expires: 10/30/2026 About the program:The Deutsche Bank Internship Program is designed to help you develop your skills through formal training and continuous support. You'll quickly gain the confidence to take on real projects by learning first-hand how and what we deliver for clients worldwide. You'll feel supported by colleagues from across our business and start to develop your professional network.About the Division:Quantitative Research & Development Labs (QRD Labs) is a research and development team within DB Group Strategic Analytics (GSA). Its central mission is to empower the sales and trading functions (and related teams) with quantitative data-driven models and tools that leverage the latest developments in the AI/ML space. You will have the opportunity to use your strong foundational knowledge in deep learning and/or natural language processing to build solutions for the business which are both practical and innovative.You'll engage with colleagues in Front Office and other areas to develop novel, high impact AI solutions for their teams. These solutions will help service our clients better and further improve the efficiency of our sales and trading desks.You'll work with a team of seasoned experts to find data-driven solutions to challenging business problems, identifying suitable data and models, developing, and evaluating prototype models rapidly and helping to accelerate the adoption of solutions in production.About the role:Our interns learn about our business through on-the-job experience. You will gain a significant understanding of the work we do, our team culture, and will develop your quantitative skills through real-life application.You may find yourself working on one large project for the entire internship or a series of smaller projects, much as you would do as a full-time member of the team. Get ready to use your quantitative and programming skills to provide impactful research and implement real solutions.You'll also be exposed to a fast-paced and agile culture giving you the opportunity to meet and engage with leaders across the organization.What we look for:You must be studying a post-graduate specialist degree (MSc or PhD) in a quantitative subject such as mathematics, engineering, physics, economics or financeYou will already have a record of outstanding academic achievement, and you're eager to continue learning at the same intensive rate. You'll thrive on working in a highly collaborative environment with some of the best minds in banking.Strong ground-up understanding of ML and AI models, from the fundamentals of machine learning to Deep Learning, with experience of its application in NLP or other domains.An ability to break down complex business problems and address them with a range of models and techniques, with strong intuition around suitability and complexity, and related trade-offs.Strong quantitative skills, e.g. statistics, probability theory, optimisation, linear algebra.Good Python and associated ML ecosystem skills; an understanding of lower-level languages is a bonus.An appreciation of different areas of finance and how they interact is useful. You will be comfortable interacting with stakeholders and colleagues across the bank.Please note that to progress onto the final stage assessment, applicants will need to attend an in-person technical test on a specified date and location, which is not flexible. More details will be shared with the successful shortlisted candidates.To be eligible for the 2027 UK Quant Internship programme you must:Complete your studies between 1st May 2026 and 30th November 2027. As the programme is due to start between May 2027 and June 2027, this means you may still be studying when you join the programme. In this case you are still eligible to join provided you have completed all of your exams before your start date and must complete your studies (any remaining coursework and have no outstanding requirements for graduation) by 30th November 2027.Have already achieved a 2:1 or First (or equivalent) in your undergraduate degree and be on track for or have already achieved a pass/merit/distinction (or equivalent) in your postgraduate degree either before you join, or by 30th November 2027.Have studied a postgraduate degree in a quantitative discipline such as mathematics, engineering, physics, computer science, economics, or financePossess no more than 12 months full-time, relevant work experience.The internship will start between May and June 2027 and will have a duration of 18 weeks.Benefits and wellbeing:Feeling healthy, engaged and well-supported, enables us to do our best work and get the most out of life outside of the office. We know that high-performing teams have different skills, backgrounds, and experiences. We collaborate, encourage and enable open dialogue and diversity of views. We build talented and diverse teams to drive business results and encourage our people to develop to their full potential. Talk to us about flexible work arrangements and other initiatives we offer.We promote good working relationships and encourage high standards of conduct and work performance. We welcome applications from talented people from all cultures, countries, races, genders, sexual orientations, disabilities, beliefs and generations and are committed to providing a working environment free from harassment, discrimination and retaliation.Visit This is DB to discover more about the culture of Deutsche Bank including Diversity, Equity & Inclusion, Leadership, Learning, Future of Work and more besides.How to apply:Whether you're fresh out of school or already have some experience, you'll find a wealth of helpful tools and information on our Employability Hub that will support you with your application, prepare for the assessment processes and adapt to a new working environment.Please visit https://careers.db.com/students-graduates/#/graduate/ to apply.Please note you may only make ONE application per recruitment season in the UK. jobs.title: Deutsche Bank Quantitative GSA Internship Programme - London - 2027 at Deutsche Bank
jobs.description: Employer: Deutsche Bank Expires: 10/30/2026 About the programme:The Deutsche Bank Internship Programme is designed to help you develop your skills through formal training and continuous support. You’ll quickly gain the confidence to take on real projects by learning first-hand how and what we deliver for clients worldwide. You’ll feel supported by colleagues from across our business and start to develop your professional network.About the Division:GSA owns and develops many cutting-edge quantitative analytics and projects. GSA started with delivering pricing and risk solutions to Sales & Trading and the majority of GSA internship topics have been around Fixed Income and Currencies (FIC) activities.The following teams are offering roles:DB Analytics is the front office cross-asset quant team in charge of the research and development of Deutsche Bank’s pricing models. The DB Analytics library is the inner mathematical layer of every DB pricing and risk management system, and it is used to price every cash and derivative transaction in rates, inflation, credit, foreign exchange, commodities, mortgages and hybrids.You should expect a challenging derivatives modeling project that includes numerical implementation and analysis. You will work under the supervision of a senior team member who covers a business area e.g. interest rate exotic options.The team puts the heaviest emphasis on stochastic calculus. You’ll need strong quantitative skills to read and analyse mathematically challenging research papers and will be required to develop an intuition on complex concepts. Solid programming skills will be needed to implement a modeling prototype in C++.Rates Desk Strats — you will use mathematical modelling and programming to help the business drive revenue through advanced risk management analytics, market data build-out, and process automation. In this collaborative role, you will partner with a wide variety of stakeholders — including Trading, Sales, Structuring, Market Risk, Technology, and Operations - while delivering a dedicated project for one of our Rates desks (spanning Linear Swaps, European Government Bonds, Non-Linear Rates, Commodities, Inflation, Hybrids & Exotics, or Quantitative Investment Strategies). To succeed, you should demonstrate strong quantitative and programming skills, a natural curiosity for financial markets, and excellent communication and collaboration abilities.You need strong quantitative & programming skills, a natural curiosity for financial markets, and excellent communication and collaboration abilities.Credit Desk Strats – you will work in a front-office, desk-aligned quantitative team supporting Deutsche Bank’s Credit Trading businesses. The role involves partnering with Trading, Structuring, Technology, Operations, and other analytics teams to solve pricing, risk, P&L, data, workflow, and platform challenges across Credit Flow, Credit Solutions, Structured Credit, Securitized Credit, Whole Loans, Distressed and related activities. Projects may include pricing and risk analytics, intraday P&L and risk tools, trader / sales / client analytics, portfolio trading automation, data-quality improvements, AI-enabled analytics, and migration to strategic platforms such as Kannon, e-Risk, IRIS, TradeGate, IMC, and SPR. You should bring strong quantitative and programming skills, attention to detail, product curiosity, and the ability to communicate effectively with trading-desk stakeholders.The team requires strong quantitative & programming skills with great attention to detail. A good understanding of financial products will give you an edge. Motivation and communication are a must as collaboration & partnership with the business is key to adopt new solutions.CB & PB Strats — is responsible for all quantitative and analytical work for Corporate Bank and Private Bank divisions. This includes pricing, funding, liquidity management, IR risk calculation and hedging, profitability measurement, capital optimization, and SVA. We build and roll out Kannon (our front office risk and pricing platform) to these divisions to support these functionalities. We work closely with Cash Management, Trade Finance and Lending, Strategic Corporate Lending in CB as well as both Wealth Management and Retail business in Private Bank. We partner with Treasury and Treasury Strats on several initiatives.Treasury Strategic Analytics supports the Treasury function in the bank and supports desks such as Pool Trading, Asset & Liability Management, Liquidity Management, Issuance, Liquidity Reserve Management, Capital Management. jobs.description: Employer: Procter & Gamble (P&G) Expires: 10/31/2026 Job LocationCINCINNATI GENERAL OFFICES Job DescriptionAre you energized by using integrative thinking to solve tough business problems, using diverse sources of knowledge from analytics to psychology? Are you an intellectually curious individual who is passionate about uncovering human needs and desires? Are you able to discover the story in all the noise and identify what really matters? If so, then a role in the Analytics & Insights (A&I) organization is for you! At P&G, we believe that diverse experiences help build strong leaders. Mobility is a key component of many management careers, providing opportunities to grow through different assignments, locations, and business challenges. Candidates should be prepared to consider relocation opportunities throughout their career as business needs and development opportunities arise. In A&I, we combine analytics and insights to directly influence business strategy, product design, pricing, media investments, retail, go to market strategy … and much more! We use our boundless curiosity to discover what consumers want, why they want it, and how we can influence them through immersive exploration, in-depth analysis, and robust research. We use state-of-the-art analytics tools to dig deep into the data, identifying key business drivers and assessing the impact of investments like advertising and in store promotions. We use big data sources and analytics to understand consumers, markets, and retailers. We conduct qualitative research to better understand consumer behavior. We answer questions like: What should our brands stand for? Who are our target shoppers? How do we best reach them? How can we create exciting in-store and online shopper experiences? And…what’s next? Our interns serve as internal business strategy consultants, whose role is to ensure that consumer and shopper analytics and insights are the foundations of our business strategy and execution. Our interns work on multi-functional business teams – with Brand Management, Finance, Sales, R&D, and others – to constantly explore new opportunities for business growth. Your key to success will be your ability to build on and combine soft skills such as curiosity, learning agility, and communication with analytical skills to convey research findings and drive actions with your key business partners across levels and functions. We believe people are endlessly fascinating and that there’s always something new to discover. One day you could be exploring human decision-making and how the brain works, and another deep diving into big data sets to create insights that shape P&G business strategies. So, here’s your opportunity! We’re looking for passionate and driven individuals to join our thriving Analytics and Insights team. jobs.title: Spring 2027 International Advocacy & Litigation Legal Internship at Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights
jobs.description: Employer: Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights Expires: 10/31/2026 Spring 2027 International Advocacy & Litigation Legal InternshipDepartment: International Advocacy & LitigationPart-time, Non-ExemptOpenings: Three*Location: Washington, DC (Hybrid) or Worldwide (Remote) Robert & Ethel Kennedy Human Rights Center is seeking Spring Legal Interns to advance the work of the International Advocacy and Litigation team for the Spring of 2027. The internship is a 10-week commitment, from January 19, 2027, to March 26, 2027. Applications are considered and positions are offered on a rolling basis, but preference will be given to applications received by 11:59 pm EST on Sunday, November 8, 2026.About the Int’l Advocacy & Litigation Team:Our team of lawyers and issue experts work hand-in-hand with local partners across the globe to create lasting social and legal change. Through bold advocacy and strategic litigation, we have freed political prisoners, upheld the rule of law in autocratic regimes, and amplified the voices of human rights defenders in some of the world’s most challenging environments. We focus on the protection of civic space, combating violence and discrimination, and demanding accountability for gross human rights violations, particularly in Africa, Asia, and Latin America. Additionally, each year we present the annual Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights Award, honoring a courageous individual whose activism embodies Robert F. Kennedy’s belief that each person has the power to make a difference and build a more just and peaceful world. Legal Intern Responsibilities: Conducting international human rights legal research and drafting memoranda in support of litigation, fact-finding reports, and advocacy materials, as well as on recent developments of thematic issues and in-country conditions relevant to the work of the Kennedy Human Rights Center; Assisting in the preparation of documents to support litigation before international mechanisms (e.g. Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights, UN Treaty Bodies), and in support of advocacy before domestic and foreign governments, international organizations, and UN special procedures;Attending and reporting on briefings, Congressional hearings, symposia, and other meetings;Monitoring sources of information on countries and issues of concern to the Kennedy Human Rights Center; and collecting, organizing, and analyzing relevant information;Working closely with International Advocacy and Litigation team members to develop long-term strategies, legal actions, and advocacy campaigns to support the RFK Human Rights Award laureates and other partners; Providing additional support to Kennedy Human Rights staff as needed. Qualifications:Applicants must have completed at least one year of law school at the start of the internship and have a well-established interest in human rights;The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated base understanding (academic/research/work experience) of regional and international human rights law; Working knowledge of the United Nations system (e.g. UN treaty bodies, special procedures, Universal Periodic Review, etc.) and/or the regional human rights mechanisms (e.g. Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights, etc.); An ability to master complex human rights issues under tight deadlines; Fluency in one of the following languages is desirable but not required: Arabic, French, Spanish or Portuguese;Strong verbal and written communication skills;Attention to detail; you’re able to spot errors and are willing to fix mistakes;Time management: you have the ability to manage multiple tasks and projects at once;High level of integrity and discretion in handling confidential information;Innovative thinking, a willingness to voice opinions, and a strong work ethic are essential; Teamwork: you are able to build positive relationships with your colleagues and are willing to help others;Ability to work with colleagues with different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives from your own.Availability and Compensation:This part-time internship will commence as early as January 19, 2027, and end by March 26, 2027, with a commitment of 15-20 hours per week.Institutional/University funding for part-time internships should cover at least $750 per month for internship allocation; Funding from Kennedy Human Rights Center is contingent on institutional/university funds not being available. Funding accessibility does not impact hiring decisions;Interns may be eligible to receive a $750 monthly stipend. How to Apply:Submit your resume, cover letter, a 3-5 page writing sample, and list of 3 professional references to intern@kennedyhumanrights.org with “Your Name + Spring 2027 Int’l Legal Internship” in the subject line heading. (Ex: Jane Doe + Spring 2027 Int’l Legal Internship)In your cover letter, please include how you heard about this role, why you’re interested in this position, and which of our team’s focus areas you are most interested in working on: Africa, Latin America, or Civic Space (global). Please be aware that many factors are considered when making your assignment, and you may not be assigned your indicated preference. Please also include whether you're accepting or applying for institutional funding for this internship and the name of the program.We know AI tools are part of how many people work and write today. That said, what we're really hoping to read is you: your real experiences, your genuine interest in this work, and your own voice. The cover letter especially is our first chance to get to know you. Generic applications are hard to act on - specific, honest ones are what get our attention.Successful writing samples will consist of a legal brief on international human rights law and standards. Please submit all application materials in English.Application Deadline: Applications are due by 11:59 pm EST on November 8, 2026. Please note that due to the high volume of applications received, Kennedy Human Rights Center will follow up with qualified candidates directly regarding the interview process. No phone calls, please. You are welcome here...Robert & Ethel Kennedy Human Rights Center is an equal opportunity employer and believes we are stronger and more effective by working internally and externally with people of all abilities, diverse backgrounds, and a range of perspectives, particularly those historically marginalized or underrepresented. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. We do not discriminate in our hiring practices, and in order to build the strongest possible workforce, actively seek a diverse applicant pool. If you're in need of an accommodation at any time during the application and hiring process please contact us by emailing your request to hr@rfkhumanrights.org with the subj. line "Accommodation Request". Examples include, but are not limited to:Having documents in alternate formats or read aloudHaving interviews in a more accessible location/format

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Commercial Construction Summer Intern at Jamerson Lewis Construction
jobs.description: Employer: Jamerson Lewis Construction Expires: 10/31/2026 Commercial Construction Summer InternshipAt Jamerson-Lewis Construction, our summer internship puts you in the middle of how buildings actually get built, from the ground up. We offer two tracks, depending on your experience: Track 1 for interns building their foundation, and Track 2 for interns ready to take on real project ownership.Track 1: General Internship Open to construction-related majors, sophomores through seniors. Over 12 weeks, you'll rotate through three sides of the business: the jobsite, the project management office, and estimating. By the end, you won't just know what a general contractor does. You'll have done it.Six weeks on-site with a SuperintendentThis is where the real learning happens. You'll work alongside the crew, not just watch from the trailer: coordinating subs and suppliers, pitching in on-site, and sitting in on progress meetings and inspections. Safety, quality, problem-solving on the fly: it's all here, and you're doing it, not just observing it.Three weeks shadowing a Project ManagerSee how a project actually gets pulled off. You'll learn scheduling, budget management, and how to keep clients, subs, and your team all moving in the same direction.Three weeks with an EstimatorGet inside the numbers. Learn to read blueprints and specs, build accurate cost estimates, and go through the real process of bid prep and contract negotiation.Track 2: Project Engineer InternshipOpen to students with at least one prior construction internship and strong references. Instead of rotating through departments, you'll be embedded on one project for the whole summer, working as a project engineer alongside our team.This is real project engineer work, not observation. You'll track submittals and RFIs, coordinate with subcontractors, help manage project documentation, and support the PM and Superintendent on the day-to-day decisions that keep a job on schedule and on budget. You'll be accountable for real deliverables on a real project.Both internships offer:Housing availableCompetitive payDirect access to our Executive Leadership teamReal project work from day oneWhichever track fits you, this is hands-on, high-trust, career-launching work. Come build something incredible with us.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Social Media Internship at Huntington Bank
jobs.description: Employer: Huntington Bank Expires: 10/31/2026 Summary: Huntington’s internship programs provide emerging talent with meaningful, hands‑on experience aligned to their area of study. Over the course of the interns’ time at Huntington, they gain exposure to key business functions across all segments of the organization. An intern’s experience should be focused on professional growth, skill development, and practical application of academic learning. Interns participate in a structured series of development opportunities, including interactions with senior leadership and career pathing insights. The experience also includes immersion in Huntington’s award‑winning culture through community involvement and team‑based activities. Internships at Huntington are designed to help students build a strong foundation for future career success while contributing to meaningful business initiatives. Internship Opportunities at Huntington: Huntington offers internship opportunities for students who are currently enrolled in an academic program and seeking practical, hands‑on experience in their field of study. Internships take place during a defined period of time and are available across all business segments. Rising juniors (Winter 2028 or Spring 2029 grads) may participate in Huntington's Foundations Program, an 8-week, regionally focused experience where students partner directly with a manager and team, contribute to meaningful projects, build professional skills, and explore career opportunities across Huntington and the financial services industry. All interns participate in a variety of developmental and professional activities designed to support learning and exposure to the organization. Depending on your school year, program components may include: Experience in day‑to‑day responsibilities related to their assigned team Exposure to broader business functions A structured schedule of professional development sessions Opportunities to engage with members of the Executive Leadership Team Discussions with senior leaders regarding career paths and Huntington’s business areas A team project focused on applying Huntington’s innovation framework to a business‑relevant problem Participation in volunteer activities and internal events aligned with Huntington’s culture Social Media Internship Overview Huntington Bank is seeking creative, curious and collaborative college students to join our Social Media Internship Program.Eligibility note: This internship is open to rising college juniors enrolled during Summer 2027 at one of the Huntington partner schools for this program: University of Michigan, University of Minnesota, West Virginia University, University of Texas, The Ohio State University, University of Mississippi, University of Alabama or Mississippi State University.This internship offers hands-on experience across the full social media content lifecycle within a highly regulated industry. Interns will join Huntington’s editorial content team and work alongside social media, brand, creative, video and production partners to learn how content moves from initial concept through creation, approval, publication and performance evaluation.Each intern will come from one of Huntington’s partner universities and bring their campus perspective into the program. Working remotely from their home communities, with hybrid in-office participation for Columbus-based interns, interns will contribute ideas, insights and content recommendations that help Huntington connect with customers, communities and university audiences across our footprint. As part of the experience, each intern will develop localized content guidance that reflects their campus, student audience and community context. Duties & Responsibilities: Collaborate with fellow interns and mentors to develop social media concepts grounded in audience needs, business goals, cultural moments and emerging platform opportunities.Participate in brainstorming, creative reviews and content planning discussions by presenting concepts, explaining recommendations and contributing constructive feedback.Work with the editorial content team member who creates and delivers Huntington’s advice and guidance newsletter to identify relevant articles and incorporate them into social plans in ways that are useful, timely and audience-aware.Create, edit, optimize and adapt content for a variety of social platforms and formats, including original photo or video content when opportunities arise and repurposed brand, event or partnership assets.Develop a localized social content toolkit, guide or plan for their Huntington partner university, helping the team understand campus culture, student needs, relevant moments and content opportunities, then present their recommendations to the brand team and other relevant Huntington stakeholders at the end of the internship.Support content planning, workflow management, project execution and performance analysis to help improve future social media content. What You'll LearnContent Strategy, Concept Development & Audience Insight: Learn how leading brands identify audience needs, generate ideas and build content strategies that support business objectives, audience engagement, relevant cultural moments and localized opportunities for Huntington partner universities.Content Creation, Storytelling & Editorial-to-Social Integration: Develop skills in social-first storytelling, content production, copywriting, editing, platform adaptation and content optimization, including how advice and guidance articles can be adapted into useful, timely social plans.Creative Pitching, Collaboration & Feedback: Gain experience presenting ideas, explaining creative rationale, communicating recommendations to peers and stakeholders, and refining work through constructive feedback and collaboration.Project Management: Understand how projects move from concept to completion through planning, timelines, approvals and stakeholder coordination.Brand Standards, Compliance & Reputational Risk: Experience how content is created and reviewed within a regulated financial services environment while balancing strong creative ideas with brand standards, business objectives, risk management and reputational considerations.Measurement & Assessment: Learn how social media content is evaluated and how performance insights are used to improve future content strategies. Required SkillsStrong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present ideas clearly.Enthusiasm for social media and a thoughtful understanding of its value, influence, challenges and responsibility as a public-facing communication channel.Creativity, curiosity and willingness to contribute new ideas.Strong organizational skills, attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.Comfort working independently in a remote environment and collaborating effectively with others.Openness to giving, receiving and incorporating constructive feedback. Preferred SkillsExperience creating content for personal, academic, volunteer, student organization, freelance or professional channels, including social media posts, video, photography, graphics, copywriting or other digital storytelling formats.Comfort using creative tools such as CapCut, Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, Final Cut Pro, in-app editing tools within social platforms or similar platforms to edit, design or adapt content.Interest in how social platforms work, including audience engagement, trends, platform best practices and the role social media can play in building connection, trust and action.Experience contributing to group projects, events, campaigns or creative initiatives, including presenting ideas, collaborating with peers and working toward a shared goal. QualificationsRising college junior enrolled during Summer 2027 at one of the Huntington partner schools for this program: University of Michigan, University of Minnesota, West Virginia University, University of Texas, The Ohio State University, University of Mississippi, University of Alabama or Mississippi State University.Pursuing a degree in Marketing, Communications, Journalism, Media, Advertising, Public Relations, Film, Digital Media or a related field. Application ProcessCandidates selected to advance in the interview process will be asked to complete a brief creative exercise demonstrating their understanding of social media audiences, content strategy and storytelling.

jobs.title: Communications Intern at Parks & Trails New York
jobs.description: Employer: Parks & Trails New York Expires: 11/01/2026 Parks & Trails New York is seeking a creative, organized, and enthusiastic Communications & Marketing Intern to support our communications and marketing efforts. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys storytelling, creating visual content, and working across a variety of projects.The Communications Intern will play an important role in promoting PTNY’s programs, events, advocacy work, and public lands. The intern will create content for social media and digital platforms while also supporting marketing campaigns, email communications, graphic design, event promotion, and other communications projects as needed.A particular focus of this position will be supporting the marketing and promotion of PTNY’s bike tours Cycle the Erie Canal & Cycle the Hudson Valley. The intern will help develop creative ways to reach new audiences, promote the tours, and research new outreach opportunities.ResponsibilitiesCreate engaging content for PTNY’s social media channels, including writing captions, designing graphics, and helping produce photo and video content.Write and edit blog posts, website content, newsletters, promotional materials, and other communications.Assist with the development and execution of marketing campaigns for bike tours, events, and other PTNY programs.Create graphics and other visual materials for social media, email, web, print, and promotional campaigns using tools such as Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, or similar platforms.Help develop and maintain social media content calendars.Support email marketing efforts, including drafting content, creating graphics, and assisting with campaign preparation. Help promote PTNY’s bike tours through social media, email, partnerships, digital outreach, and other marketing channels.Research potential audiences, promotional opportunities, media outlets, community partners, and other avenues for expanding PTNY’s reach.Assist with event promotion and communications before, during, and after PTNY programs and events.Help collect and organize photos, videos, stories, and other content.Monitor social media trends and identify creative opportunities to increase engagement and reach.Provide general communications and marketing support as needed, including occasional administrative or research projects. QualificationsRequired:Strong writing and editing skills with excellent attention to detail.Comfortable creating content for social media and other digital platforms.Experience or demonstrated interest in graphic design and visual storytelling.Familiarity with Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, or similar design tools.Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.Ability to work independently while also taking direction and collaborating with a team.Enthusiasm for trails, outdoor recreation, cycling, parks, or connecting people with New York’s natural and cultural resources. Preferred:Experience managing or creating content for social media accounts.Experience with photography, videography, or basic video editing.Familiarity with email marketing platforms such as Mailchimp.Experience with website content management systems.Interest in marketing, communications, public relations, nonprofit organizations, tourism, or outdoor recreation.Familiarity with New York’s trails, parks, cycling networks, or outdoor recreation communities. What You’ll GainThis internship provides hands-on experience in nonprofit communications and marketing, with opportunities to work across content creation, graphic design, digital marketing, event promotion, and audience engagement. The intern will have the opportunity to take ownership of projects while gaining experience promoting programs and initiatives that connect people across New York with public lands and outdoor recreation.Ideal CandidateWe’re looking for someone who is a strong writer, a creative thinker, and someone who can take a rough idea and turn it into a social post, graphic, blog article, email campaign, or marketing concept. The ideal candidate is comfortable learning new tools, willing to tackle a variety of projects, and excited by the opportunity to help tell the story of New York’s public lands.HoursPart-time, approximately 20 hours/week, beginning in Nov 2026 and running through June 2027. Schedules can be flexible in terms of days and times but must be within regular work week hours (M-F, 8-5). Work LocationWork will primarily be remote, with a preference for candidates local to the Albany, NY area. Interns work closely with staff in a friendly, hard-working, casual atmosphere with the option for a mix including in-person hours.Compensation$18 per hour, may be used for college internship requirements.Please send a resume and cover letter to careers@ptny.org with the subject line “ASI Comms Position.” Early applications are encouraged and will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We will prioritize candidates who apply by November 1, 2026.Our organization is working to be an anti-racist, safe, and inclusive organization. BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, people of color) individuals, women, immigrants, people with disabilities, people of marginalized sexual orientations or gender identities, and people with low-income backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply. We also encourage individuals belonging to the above groups who meet some, but not all, of the position requirements to apply.Hiring Process & TimelineInitial candidates will be invited for a brief screening call set up via email.Selected candidates will then be invited for a remote interview. Those invited for an interview will be notified within a week to two weeks of the phone screening.*Due to the high volume of applications received, we will only contact those selected to move forward in the screening process.

jobs.title: College Financial Representative at Northwestern Mutual - Cranberry Twp (Northern Pittsburgh)
jobs.description: Employer: Northwestern Mutual - Cranberry Twp (Northern Pittsburgh) Expires: 11/01/2026 College Financial Representatives in the internship program at Northwestern Mutual Cranberry Township are provided guidance, connection, and a framework for building an integrated financial planning practice from the ground up. Our college financial representatives, who come from varying academic backgrounds and experiences, have the unique opportunity to build a financial planning practice while engaging local and nationwide experts, selling exclusive financial products, and having the support of a Fortune 500 company. You will have the opportunity to build your confidence, develop a professional network, and help people achieve financial freedom. Here, hard work pays off! Our internship program mimics our full-time Financial Representative career, allowing you to: Learn how to prospect and network to build your business and client base Develop and execute on a business strategy Call on potential clients and set meetings to understand their financial goals Prepare plans and offer useful recommendations Gain exposure to proprietary planning software platforms Engage in weekly coaching, training, and development meetings Get licensed with your Life, Accident, and Health insurance license Build life skills that create future career opportunities As a Northwestern Mutual College Financial Representative, you can expect a flexible schedule to work around your life and your classes. With the option to participate in our internship program year-round, you can continue to grow your practice and obtain support for registrations and certifications such as the Series 6 & 63 or CFP®. Get inspired at local and national recognition events, earn access to leadership programs, and collaborate with experts in our business. In fact, you’ll find diverse resources across our culture to ensure that you experience personal and professional growth in this program. With interest, eligible students have an opportunity to interview for a full-time Financial Representative or Advisor role upon graduation. Are you a fit for this internship? Full-time student; juniors and seniors preferred Entrepreneurial ambitions and curiosity for sales Highly involved on campus (leader, athlete, campus orgs, student government, etc.) Excellent time-management skills Interest in financial literacy and planning tools Business savvy and desire to increase critical thinking abilities Compensation & Benefits Performance-based earnings and revenue Learning and Development Incentives (up to $1000/month, not inclusive of earned commissions) Productivity Bonuses Support for insurance licensing (life, health, DI, LTC) Support for SIE, Series 6, Series 63 registrations (eligibility required) About Us For over 165 years, we have helped our clients spend their lives living through comprehensive and innovative financial planning. We combine the expertise of our financial professionals with personalized digital experience and industry-leading products to give our clients the ability to successfully navigate their financial lives. Our tailored approach includes multiple financial strategies—insurance, investments, and annuities—built to reinforce each other, keeping our clients consistently on track to meet goal after goal. We lead with unmatched financial strength and access to the best products and services for our clients. Our Financial Representatives and College Financial Representatives are valued partners and proud business owners. As such, they are considered independent contractors1 for income tax purposes, and a "statutory employee" for Federal Insurance Contributions Act (FICA) tax purposes. As a company, we value an inclusive and belonging workplace where everyone’s unique viewpoints bring new successes. We strive to create teams that reflect our customers and communities, fostering an environment where all employees are welcomed, valued, and heard. Why join Northwestern Mutual: Fortune 500® company (June 2024) Top 100 Internship Programs, Yello x WayUp (2024) 5.1+ million clients and growing2 Unsurpassed financial strength with total company assets of $366 billion3 Forbes' Best Employers for Diversity (2023) Best Place to Work for LGBTQ+ Equality- Human Rights Campaign Corporate Equality Index (2023) 1 Northwestern Mutual College Financial Representatives are Independent Contractors whose income is based on production. If offered to apply for approval of an intern contract to become a Northwestern Mutual College Financial Representative, a national criminal background check is required. Should the background check results provide information which would not allow someone to work for Northwestern Mutual, approval to contract will be withdrawn. 2 As of December 31, 2023 3 Among U.S. life insurers. Ratings are for The Northwestern Mutual Life Insurance Company and Northwestern Long Term Care Insurance Company, as of the most recent review and report by each rating agency. Ratings as of: 08/24 (Aaa, Moody’s Investors Service), 08/23 (A++, A.M. Best Company), 07/24 (AAA, Fitch Ratings), 04/24 (AA+, S&P Global Ratings). Ratings are subject to change. Total company assets as of June 30, 2024.
